To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

A60, a cytoplasmic antigen from M. tuberculosis, was immunogenic when given to mice in Freund's incomplete Adjuvant, but that the protection it afforded against challenge with virulent M. tuberculosis was less than that given by BCG.

1) the A60 protein can be used to vaccinate mice against tuberculosis; 2) the vaccine is more effective when administered in Freund's incomplete Adjuvant (FCA); 3) the vaccine is less effective than BCG; 4) the vaccine is effective when administered by aerosol; 5) the vaccine is not protective against a challenge with M. tuberculosis H37Ra.
A60 is a promising candidate for use as a vaccine to protect against tuberculosis in man.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new vaccine for tuberculosis.
the development of a vaccine to protect against tuberculosis.
the identification, purification and characterization of the antigens of M. bovis BCG and their evaluation as vaccine candidates against tuberculosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the A60 protein is immunogenic and can induce protection in mice against challenge with M. tuberculosis.
the adjuvant-free A60 protein is not a suitable candidate for use as a vaccine against tuberculosis in mice.
A60 is a promising vaccine candidate for tuberculosis but that it is less effective than BCG and requires further development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the A60 protein of M. tuberculosis and BCG can induce protective immunity in mice against challenge with M. tuberculosis Erdmann, but that the response is less than that seen with the whole BCG vaccine.
immunization with A60 in FIA is not as protective as BCG vaccination.
A60 is a useful vaccine candidate but that the adjuvant used in this study was not optimal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antigen A60 of Mycobacterum bovis BCG is capable of eliciting a protective immune response against tuberculosis in mice.
the A60 protein can elicit a significant degree of protection against tuberculosis in mice.
the antigen A60 is a good candidate for a subunit vaccine against tuberculosis.
